doc: P2.12 behaviour-profile keyword rules. Sources: docs/01_GAME_DESIGN.md §2 (the harness tags every player message into the profile counters with a cheap classifier pass plus keyword rules — this file is the keyword half of the harness that reads the player's own words) and §4 (the path formulas read control and apathy, tags the model's 17 `read` labels cannot express, plus broken_promises, flattery_rejected and ignored_questions). How a rule fires, one contribution per counter per message — a message is one behaviour, not a keyword count, so keyword bumps stay comparable to the read-table's single bumps: control = the player orders her around (one whole-word imperative phrase, never a generic 'you will' / 'you must' / 'i said', which are ordinary sentences); apathy = a dismissal that IS the message, or a reply of at most short_reply_words words that asks nothing and is not exempt (docs/01 §4.4 counts 'short replies' as a HOLLOW trigger). 'Is the message' is what dismissal_max_words enforces: a line longer than that is an engaged line, so a phrase inside it ('I don't care about her, I care about you.') is not a dismissal. A question asks and is therefore never a dismissal, and a terse reply to her direct question is an answer, not a dismissal — answering is not ignoring (docs/01 §5 T15). Ambiguous one-word stems ('ok', 'fine', 'sure', 'cool', 'lol') are deliberately not phrases: the short-reply cap catches them standing alone, and containment would only catch them inside warm lines; flattery_rejected = the player flatters her (flattery stems in the message) AND her own reply rejects it (rejection markers in the beats' say) — the TSUN 'mild rudeness she wins' dynamic; ignored_questions = her previous turn asked a direct question (question_in) and this reply is dismissive (the apathy rule) — docs/01 §5 T15 remains the model-detected authority and the trigger engine's bump is additive. Matching is case-insensitive and whole-word after punctuation is folded to spaces, so a phrase never fires inside a longer word; exemptions match as whole words too, so 'no' never exempts 'nothing' and 'sorry' does exempt 'I'm sorry'. broken_promises is deliberately absent: docs/01 §5 I15 makes a promise an engine fact, so the trigger engine calls GameState.bump_profile(&"broken_promises") — P2.10 wires that trigger. An empty or invalid file degrades to no keyword bumps (the read labels and the path formulas still work), never to a guessed bump. Sensitivity (docs/01 §4): no real disorder is named in this file.
